about: THE PLACES ARE TEMPLATES (WORLD THIRTEEN 11/11, VAMILY rules 429(a)(c)(f), 430; ask lines 504, 506, 507). The 15 place boards (slices/fight_ground/fight_ground.json boards place_*, their layouts kept whole: every block, its terrain, its cover, its lights) are templates the map's generator places wherever that kind of place lands on a valley. A board is 20 x 15 fight tiles of 12 m; a map block is 3 x 3 of them (36 m), so a template stands on 7 x 5 map blocks, and every block of its kinds under it is a cell of it: the fight there is fought on that board, the cell's own three by three tiles under the spot it starts. Nothing of a board is thrown away or redrawn; only where it stands is new (rule 430).
source: records/target/bb/ours.json place_boards (each place's kinds, its landmark and field: the fight's); this file adds where and how many

fields.board: the fight_ground.json board the template is
fields.name: the place's name (place_boards)
fields.kinds: the map kinds it stands on: the fight's own place_boards districts, word for word (the gate holds them together)
fields.per_valley: the most of it on one valley
fields.min_cells: the fewest blocks of its kinds under a footprint for it to stand there (a rare place, one block is enough)
fields.spacing: the least distance in blocks between two of it on one valley (0: one only)
fields.mirror: the board may stand mirrored east to west: false for every place while the fight stands a named board unmirrored (the map and the fight must show the same place; 11/11, __THE_CUT__)
fields.slack: how many blocks short of the best footprint still count as as good (the valley's hash picks among them): a narrow place, the Strip, then stands at a different part of its board on different valleys, so every part of the board is used (rule 430)

how: For each template, rarest first (the order below): every footprint on the valley is scored by how many blocks of its kinds it covers; the best stands, then the next best that overlaps no template already standing and keeps its spacing, until per_valley or min_cells. Ties go to the valley's own hash, so the same valley always stands the same places. Pure: no roll of the valley moves.
